name: Palm Beach Reef (Palm Beach Artificial Reef, Gold Coast, Queensland)

confidence.reason: The outline is read from a vertical aerial photo with a scale bar and north arrow and matches the City of Gold Coast GIS polygon of the installed reef to 0.55 m (area 11,972 vs 11,942 m2); the same size, shape and ~45-degree skew to the shore appear in an independent drawing (ICCE 2022 Fig 1) and the rock is visible on 2025 satellite imagery inside that outline. Length (162 m) agrees with the quoted 160 m; the soft spots are the '80 m wide' label (91 m maximum, 74 m average), an undated aerial whose survey contours are not labelled as design or as-built, and only a quarter to a third of the rock being visible on satellite.
factors: plan-view aerial with scale bar and north arrow: scale 8.50 px/m re-measured (tick lines x = 26 / 239 / 451), north-up confirmed by a free fit to the council polygon (rotation 0.04 deg, no anisotropy: sx 1.000, sy 0.998)

City of Gold Coast GIS polygon (OBJECTID 4638, status INSV) agrees: IoU 0.996, Hausdorff 0.55 m, area +0.25 %. Probably the same survey/design data as the Bluecoast contours, so this fixes scale, orientation and position but is not an independent check of the rock
independent drawing (ICCE 2022 Fig 1 icon, scaled with 4 landmarks): area 12,017 m2 (+0.6 % vs council), 162 x 92 m, long axis 110.8 deg
rock visible on georeferenced Esri imagery (2025-12-01) inside the polygon, but only 25-38 % of the footprint (shoreward side); the rest is shown by the aerial and the contours

the aerial is undated and un-georeferenced (position = council polygon); contour lines are unlabelled (design vs as-surveyed not stated); outer line sits 3-4 m outside the dark rock on the N/NW edge and the rock spills 2-3 m beyond it on the S/SE edge
shoreline direction 334.3 +-2 deg (re-measured: 335.3 on Esri z18, 337-339 on the OSM coastline), so angles to the shore are good to ~+-3 deg

length 162 m vs 160 m text (+1.4 %); width label 80 m vs 91.3 m maximum / 73.8 m mean (+14 % / -8 %); offshore 270 m in the text vs 225 m (toe) to the waterline - the text is measured from the beach/dune edge (OSM coastline gives 279 m)

design_version.drawn: The reef as built in 2019 (rock placed May-Sept 2019, engineering certification Sept 2019): outer contour of the Bluecoast/Nearmap aerial = City of Gold Coast asset polygon (status INSV) = toe footprint, plus the innermost contour (a 59 x 6 m slot at 105 deg, matching the 60 m crest at 105 deg of the 2015 design). The aerial carries no date.
design_version.why_this_one: It is the built structure: status INSV in the City of Gold Coast asset register (BOULDER, 160 x 80 m, 11,942 m2), same outline as the contours in Bluecoast's aerial, and the oblique June-2020 photo (EPW Sept 2020) and the 'final survey of the completed reef' (ICCE 2022 Fig 4) show the same rounded mound. EPW 2020 says the structure was finalised and certified in Sept 2019 and its later condition is 'comparable to the as-constructed certification report'; Prenzler et al. (ICCE 2022) report no significant movement or settlement. It supersedes the 2014-15 concept (Mortensen et al.), which was larger and further offshore; Raised Water Research notes the reef was moved 50 m closer to shore during design to save rock.

alternatives_seen.what: Concept design SCS B (2014/15): max length 175 m, max width 144 m, footprint 21,394 m2, volume 53,319 m3, crest -1.5 m, orientation 105 deg, offshore toe 560 m offshore in 11.4 m depth (also SCS A 309 x 154 m / 96,248 m3 and SCS C 142 x 138 m / 37,112 m3)
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: Concept stage only (oblique 3D render, not traceable). The detailed design (Royal HaskoningDHV Design Reference Report) refined the location and dimensions; the built reef is ~270 m offshore with a 11,942 m2 footprint. The 144 m width on Royal HaskoningDHV's page is the concept SCS B maximum width.

alternatives_seen.what: Earlier text-derived schematic mound (07_scale/reefs/palm-beach-gold-coast.footprint.json): 160 x 80 m, area 9,678 m2, long axis alongshore
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: Schematic from text only. The traced plan shows the long axis ~45 deg to the shoreline and an area of 11,942 m2.

alternatives_seen.what: Gemini chevron (9 vertices, apex seaward, 12,800 m2 gross / 9,100 m2 net, long axis alongshore)
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: No source image; centroid-aligned IoU with the traced outline is only 0.52 (mirror allowed).

alternatives_seen.what: 2004 reef proposal near 21st Avenue (community no-reef campaign)
Concept design 'SCS B' as shown in the Raised Water Research 'Design on the left, results on the right' figure (175 m / 144 m labels, slopes 1/2 - 1/15) next to the multibeam survey of the built reef
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: Concept render (oblique, no scale); the built reef is a different, rounded-rectangular mound. Confirms that the 144 m on Royal HaskoningDHV's page is the concept width.

design_version.page_note: The drawing shows the reef as built in 2019 (toe outline from the City of Gold Coast asset register and Bluecoast's aerial). The 2014-15 concept design was larger (175 x 144 m, 21,394 m2) and sited further offshore. No extension, repair, damage or removal has been reported; the 2022-23 monitoring papers describe the reef as stable and the rock is still visible on Esri imagery of 2025-12-01. The sources do not say whether the aerial's contour lines are design or as-surveyed lines.

canonical.frame: metres; origin = foot of the perpendicular from the reef-outline centroid onto the waterline fitted to the 2025-12-01 Esri imagery; +x alongshore toward 334.3 deg (NNW); +y offshore (toward 64.3 deg, ENE)

distance_offshore_detail_m.note: measured perpendicular to the fitted waterline; the dry-sand / dune edge lies landward of the waterline, which is one way the quoted approx. 270 m can arise

canonical.handedness_note: x (toward 334.3 deg) and y (toward 64.3 deg) run clockwise on a north-up map. Draw with +x to the right and +y pointing DOWN the screen (shore at the top, sea at the bottom); with +y up the reef would be mirrored.
canonical.rounding_note: Verified 2026-10-05 by an explicit rotation of the s7 polygon (centroid at y = 305.0): all vertices agree with polygons_m to a constant 0.30 m in y (the polygons_m centroid sits at y = 304.7); extents differ by 0.3 m. Left unchanged. geom.py make-canonical was NOT used for this block, so the 2026-10-05 rotation-sign bug does not apply.

geo.method: s7 pixels -> metres with the scale bar (8.5 px/m), north up (arrow), translated onto the City of Gold Coast polygon s1 (best translation by IoU search = 0,0 m) and converted through a local azimuthal-equidistant projection to WGS84. Position accuracy ~1-2 m relative to the council data; the Esri-visible rock sits inside it (consistent to ~5 m).
geo.grid_note: The aerial is aligned to MGA56 grid north; grid convergence here is -0.22 deg, so true bearings of lines measured on the aerial differ by 0.2 deg (immaterial). geo.polygons_latlon vs the council polygon converted to WGS84: Hausdorff 0.63 m, IoU 0.995.
